questions.q: What is Jaffle Shop leadership actually asking for when they say they want a "governed, production-grade" analytics platform?
options: A more colorful set of dashboards
Five concrete things: access control, tests, documentation/lineage, a repeatable ingestion process, and a CI/CD gate before anything ships
A bigger Snowflake warehouse so queries run faster
A replacement for dbt written in a different language
questions.explain: The ask unpacks into five concrete gaps — RBAC, tests, docs/lineage, scheduled ingestion, and a CI/CD gate — not a vague call for "better analytics."

questions.q: Why is "nobody knows if a number is still right" a governance problem rather than a dashboard-design problem?
options: It isn't a real problem worth solving
Because the underlying issue is no tests, no lineage, and no one outside the data team able to verify what a model depends on — a prettier chart doesn't fix any of that
Dashboards are always wrong regardless of governance
It can only be fixed by hiring more analysts
questions.explain: A trustworthy number depends on tests catching bad data and lineage making dependencies visible — neither is a visual design concern.

questions.q: Which chapter in this capstone is responsible for closing the "a bad change ships straight to the dashboard" gap?
options: Chapter 2 — Snowflake Foundations
Chapter 6 — CI/CD for the dbt Project
Chapter 1 — Scoping the Production Analytics Platform
Chapter 5 — Python Ingestion Layer
questions.explain: Chapter 6 builds the GitHub Actions workflow and the merge gate that stops a bad change before it reaches production.

questions.q: Why does this capstone assume stg_jaffle_shop__customers and the existing marts already exist, rather than rebuilding them from Lesson 1?
options: Because dbt models can't be rebuilt once created
Because this is the Advanced tier, building on staging/mart work already done in the Beginner and Intermediate tiers, and spends its time on the governance layer those tiers didn't cover
Because Jaffle Shop's raw data no longer exists
Because Snowflake doesn't allow re-running dbt run on existing models
questions.explain: The Beginner and Intermediate tiers already cover ref(), staging, and basic marts — this tier's job is the governance and production layer around that existing work.

questions.q: What does "blast radius" refer to in the context of this lesson's governance problems?
options: The physical size of a Snowflake warehouse
How far a single change's effects can reach before something — a test, a lineage graph, a CI check — catches or limits it
The number of employees affected by a company reorganization
A Snowflake billing term for compute credits consumed
questions.explain: Blast radius describes how far a change can propagate unnoticed — the whole point of tests, docs, and CI is shrinking that radius.
